gloss: sense of despair; feeling of hopelessness

definitions.gloss: sense of despair; feeling of hopelessness
definitions.explanation: The subjective feeling or emotional experience of despair. Adds the nuance of a felt sensation to the concept of despair (絶望), emphasizing the emotional weight.

examples.japanese: {深|ふか}い{絶望感|ぜつぼうかん}に{襲|おそ}われた。
examples.english: I was overcome by a deep sense of despair.

examples.japanese: {何|なに}をしても{無駄|むだ}だという{絶望感|ぜつぼうかん}が{広|ひろ}がった。
examples.english: A feeling of hopelessness spread — a sense that nothing would work.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}{終了|しゅうりょう}{間際|まぎわ}に{逆転|ぎゃくてん}されて、{絶望感|ぜつぼうかん}に{包|つつ}まれた。
examples.english: The opposing team scored a comeback just before the end of the game, and we were enveloped in despair.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {絶望|ぜつぼう} (despair) + {感|かん} (feeling, sense). The suffix {感|かん} turns the abstract concept of despair into a word for the subjective emotional experience. This pattern is productive in Japanese: {孤独感|こどくかん} (sense of loneliness), {達成感|たっせいかん} (sense of achievement), etc.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {絶望感|ぜつぼうかん}に{襲|おそ}われる (to be seized by despair)
- {絶望感|ぜつぼうかん}に{包|つつ}まれる (to be enveloped in despair)
- {深|ふか}い{絶望感|ぜつぼうかん} (deep sense of despair)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {絶望|ぜつぼう}: despair — the state or concept itself, without the emphasis on felt sensation
- {失望感|しつぼうかん}: sense of disappointment — less intense than {絶望感|ぜつぼうかん}
